context: The Technical Design schema editor currently creates an automatic backup file every time the schema is saved (which happens on every change due to auto-save). The prompt requests removing automatic backups while keeping only the manual backup button. This questionnaire clarifies implementation details for this change.

questions.question-text: Should the manual backup button also validate the schema before creating a backup, or should it backup the current state regardless of validation status?

options.label: Validate before backup - Only create backup if schema is valid
options.pros: Ensures all backups are guaranteed to be valid schemas, prevents backing up broken states, cleaner backup history
options.cons: User cannot create a backup of work-in-progress that doesn't yet validate, might lose work if they need to close the editor with invalid schema

options.label: Backup without validation - Always create backup regardless of validation status
options.pros: User can save work-in-progress states, flexibility to backup even incomplete work, no data loss risk
options.cons: Backup directory may contain invalid schemas, user needs to be aware which backups are valid

options.label: Validate and warn - Create backup but show validation warnings if invalid
options.pros: Best of both worlds - allows backing up invalid states while informing user of issues, flexible and safe
options.cons: Slightly more complex implementation, user must acknowledge warnings

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option C provides the best user experience by allowing backups of any state while keeping users informed about validation issues. This matches the pattern already used in the auto-save function which saves with warnings.

questions.question-text: Should the UI provide any confirmation or success message after creating a manual backup, and if so, should it include the backup file path?

options.label: Show detailed message with full backup path
options.pros: User knows exactly where the backup was saved, easy to locate the file if needed immediately, transparent
options.cons: Path might be too long for status message, could clutter UI with technical details

options.label: Show simple success message only (e.g., 'Backup created successfully')
options.pros: Clean UI, less clutter, backup location is already known (backups folder), sufficient feedback
options.cons: User doesn't know exact filename, would need to check backups folder to find latest

options.label: Show message with just the filename and timestamp
options.pros: Balance between detail and clarity, filename with timestamp is most useful info, cleaner than full path
options.cons: User still needs to know backups folder location to find the file

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option C provides useful information (filename with timestamp) without overwhelming the user with the full path. This matches the current pattern where the backup path is shown in the status message, but a filename-only message is cleaner and more user-friendly.

questions.question-text: The auto-save function is still useful for preventing data loss during editing. Should we keep auto-save but remove only the automatic backup from it?

options.label: Keep auto-save, remove automatic backup - Best of both worlds
options.pros: Schema is still automatically saved to disk on changes (no data loss), but no backup clutter from every tiny change, user can manually backup at meaningful checkpoints
options.cons: None significant - this is the most logical interpretation of the prompt

options.label: Remove auto-save entirely - Require manual save
options.pros: User has full control over when saves happen, no unexpected file operations
options.cons: Risk of data loss if user forgets to save, poor user experience, breaks existing workflow, not what the prompt asks for

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A is the correct interpretation of the prompt requirement. The issue is not with auto-save itself, but with the automatic backup that happens on every save. Removing the backup from auto-save while keeping the auto-save feature preserves the good user experience while solving the backup clutter problem.
